title: Ack-window hysteresis to prevent multi-charge on retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: At high tail latencies and intermittent network partitions, customers have observed duplicate billing events for a single logical request when retries or reconnects cause multiple ingest acknowledgements to be processed. Root cause analysis shows a race between the ingest acknowledgement path and the final consumption commit, combined with a short ack-window that allows rapid re-acknowledgement to be treated as distinct billable events.

Proposal: Implement an ack-window hysteresis layer in the ingest proxy + metering pipeline that enforces a short, sequenced grace period during which subsequent acknowledged attempts for the same logical request are deduplicated at billing boundaries. Design goals: prevent multi-charge in common retry scenarios, retain low-latency happy path, limit memory/coordination overhead, and support existing usage accounting guarantees.

High-level approach:
1) Sequenced lease token: augment existing client tokens with a lightweight monotonic sequence (or client-provided nonce) when available. Server assigns a short-lived lease window id for each ingest that is used to bind meter credits for the duration of the ack-window.
2) Hysteresis window semantics: for 5s (configurable per-customer tier) after the first ack is recorded, additional acks for the same logical request are mapped to the same consumption record and ignored for billing. If an acknowledgement arrives after the window, normal billing rules apply.
3) Idempotent commit shadow: the consumption commit path will accept (lease_id, seq) tuples and perform an atomic upsert into the consumption ledger. If a record already exists with matching key and non-stale lease_id, commit is treated as no-op.
4) Edge behavior: clients behind unreliable networks can re-send with same nonce; the proxy will try to preserve the original lease_id in its retry fingerprint header. If the proxy restarts, we fall back to reconciliation sweep (see monitoring/migration).
5) Back-compat: existing clients without sequence support fall back to a short server-side generated nonce and best-effort dedupe for the hysteresis window. This preserves safety while requiring no immediate client change.
acceptance_criteria: No increase in p95 request latency >1ms on the happy path after deploying hysteresis
End-to-end unit test coverage for ingest ack deduplication across retries
E2E infra test that simulates TCP resets + retries shows single billing event per logical request
Dashboard and alert for >0.1% of requests with "multi-charge" reconciliation during initial rollout
Migration playbook validated: can toggle hysteresis via runtime flag per-tenant
updates: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Spike complete. Implemented PoC in ingest-proxy that attaches server-lease-id and verifies dedupe in-memory for 30s. Observed no regressions in throughput at 1000rps test. Recorded microbenchmarks attached.

2025-02-18 - Ethan Morrison: Design review with Payments and Runtime teams. Agreed on 5s default window, per-tenant override, and ledger upsert contract. Payments requested explicit reconciliation metric 'reconciled_multi_charge_count'.

2025-02-25 - Claire Nguyen (Payments): Raised edge-case where cross-shard requests may create two distinct ledger entries if the sequence is not propagated. Action: add replication-safe id prefix and include shard affinity in lease token format.

2025-03-01 - Ethan Morrison: Started implementation of atomic upsert using consumption-ledger v2 API (feature flagged). Writing integration tests and adding dashboard panels for 'lease_window_hits' and 'late_ack_buckets'.
notes: Trade-offs: longer hysteresis windows increase dedupe coverage but may delay legitimate replays leading to undercharging during windows; we mitigate by keeping windows short and surfacing 'late ack' events to Payments. Operational controls: runtime flag per-tenant, telemetry for lease collisions, and a reconciliation job to detect rare duplicates older than the window. Next steps: complete ledger upsert tests, add client SDK patch for optional nonce propagation, and schedule staged rollout (start with internal and low-traffic tenants).
